scope: Declare existing Vercel metadata directory before provider linking and retain safe classification of tracked dirty changes without exempting source modifications.
riskAnalysis: Hosted c6 proves tracked dirty source, not the exact changed file. Official provider ignore-update behavior and an actual Git reproduction justify adding the missing .vercel line; all dirty tracked changes still fail before packaging. Three boolean diagnostics expose no source or credential contents.

threatModel.assets: Repository source confidentiality, provider credentials, owner/task/release identities, historical receipts, counted dispatch, public application assets and shutdown state.
threatModel.trustBoundaries: Tracked immutable Git blobs to private build asset; source policy to untrusted model; owner browser to existing API/CAS; automated Chief hypothesis versus independently authenticated acceptance.
threatModel.abuseCases: Private/static source exposure, data exports, forged source bytes, stale cursors, substituted workspace/model/task, extra stages/calls, resealed historical receipts, source leakage after account changes, credential extraction and fabricated acceptance.
threatModel.mitigations: Central path/content policy, exact blob hashes, private function include outside public-dist, linked asset graph, original source packet and attempt/request/result hashes, Chief-only one-time grant/count/Response, no tools/test profile, scoped UI clearing and existing cleanup.

defects.rootCause: Provider linking can append the missing exact .vercel ignore entry, conflicting with the newly enforced clean tracked-source precondition.
defects.detectionGap: Original generic failure hid the build phase; corrected diagnostics proved DIRTY but not old changed filenames. Local build had not exercised provider preparation.
defects.regression: Actual temporary Git append triggers DIRTY with gitignoreChanged true, then committed exact metadata entry makes provider operation a no-op. Source modifications remain rejected before output mutation.
defects.historicalPrevention: Preserve lost-path uncertainty, use provider-prepared build fixtures, and retain exact source checks plus non-sensitive change classification.

rollback: Keep qualified381 feature alias and paid disabled. Revoke any later task authority, preserve failed deployment and original checkpoint, and repair only through reviewed feature commits. Production/main untouched.

negativePaths.malformed-response: Untrusted build exception messages are never rendered; fixed phase and closed uppercase code only. Existing provider response validation unchanged.
negativePaths.stale-state: Dirty or substituted Git source remains rejected; recovery pins one historical commit and original exact blobs, never a wildcard or stale approval.
negativePaths.concurrency: Existing owner CAS and serial sequence/grant checks; immutable packets and paged read-only retrieval; no parallel paid attempts.
negativePaths.cancellation: Existing controller disconnect, cancellation, emergency stop and approval/consent revocation remain; no new executor or generated-code privileges.
negativePaths.worker-interruption: One bounded provider stage uses existing cleanup; absence of a valid receipt is never model or workflow success. No Sandbox worker launched.
negativePaths.api-outage: Unknown acknowledgments keep existing durable local journals; no paid or configuration retry; restore current UI controls without displaying late foreign results.
negativePaths.authorization-denial: Non-owner/cross-workspace and substituted task denied; Chief-only one-count/one-Response limits; generic Ops fixture execution denied; implementation/tests/publication unavailable.
negativePaths.spending-limit: Existing owner-directed provider-billing monitoring unchanged; no new internal financial cap, no invoice reconciliation claims, counting and interrupted usage uncertainty preserved.
negativePaths.partial-execution: Usage survives schema failure; failure closes grants and attempts without fabricated artifacts. Chief inspect/hold is an honest one-stage result, not completed Specialist/QA/Auditor work.

proactiveReview.architecture: Reuse existing owner controller, transport, journal, counting, grants, consent and sequences; shared Git snapshot reader adds source coverage without replacing orchestration.
proactiveReview.dependencies: Built-in Node Git/zlib/fs only; no new provider, infrastructure, credentials or broad file execution. Public static assets are linked from existing frontend roots.
proactiveReview.threats: Independent reviewers reproduced privacy, crossscope UI and historical forgery counterexamples; mitigations preserve source/identity/authority separation.
proactiveReview.failureModes: Real controller tests exposed existing JSON-string versus raw-file hash domains; corrected only expected assignment hashing, never weaken exact source validation.
proactiveReview.faultInjection: Unsafe paths, secret-like data, symlinks/gitlinks, forged bytes, stale query cursors, empty/resealed attempts, unauthorized generic execution, extra-call approval and malformed provider output.
proactiveReview.independentChallenge: Existing independent Work QA and Engineering Auditor inspect exact source, test original counterexamples and retain signed hash attestations. This is technical review, not business acceptance.
proactiveReview.recovery: Preserve381 qualified Preview until successor is READY, mutate feature alias once after durable marker, verify exact runtime and cleanup before live Chief dispatch. No config refresh or credential rewrite.
proactiveReview.readiness: 26source/build checks pass; independent narrow review, incremental verified-ancestor preflight and local exact build precede next push. Actual successful hosted build remains required.
